audit.whatIsWrong: THREE FABRICATED ABILITY NAMES. (1) "Twofold Hunt" — used as the matchup's tracked cooldown in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, loading, focus.text, phases[3].why, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.trading, breakdown.spikes, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.difficulty, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[5].t, report[9].t, report[10].t, report[12].t and report[13].t. It is not an ability; the blink is Across the Veil (W). "Twofold" belongs to her Q, Twofold Hex. (2) "Feathered Step" for her W in spikes[0].text, early, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1]. (3) "The Weight of Worlds" for her E in spikes[0].text — the real name is The Weirding, and it is not a pull. FOURTH ERROR: "E stun" for Blunt Force Trauma in whys[3], whys[5], spikes[2].text, mid, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] — Dr. Mundo has no stun. FIFTH: "Q cleaver for the slow + HP refund" in tradeGood, breakdown.early, breakdown.trading, report[3].t and dosFull[1].d — Infected Bonesaw has no heal.
audit.why: From Riot's text: Twofold Hex (900 range, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s) fires a missile that CURSES enemies, and the recast drags the curses back toward her, damaging anyone in the path — it does not bounce off passive marks. Across the Veil (700 range, 22/21/20/19/18s) leaps and turns her INVISIBLE on landing with bonus move speed. The Weirding (825 range, 15/14/13/12/11s) is a blast that damages and slows, then hops her backward — no pull. Between Worlds (140/120/100s) leaps, shockwaves, then leaves a slow area she can teleport across. Spirit Abjuration heals her off spirits exorcised from everyone she damages, which is why chip-trading refills her. The decisive Mundo-side fact, flagged by the mirror and absent here: Heart Zapper only heals if its burst connects, so her E hop out of 325 range denies the heal outright.
audit.corrected: All four fake names replaced with Across the Veil, Twofold Hex, The Weirding and Between Worlds; the stun and the Q heal removed everywhere.

audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] and full phases[].side gave Levels 1, 4-5 and 6 to "Skill" while whys[0], whys[2] and whys[4] call them Aurora's, and whys[1]/whys[2] gave Levels 2 and 3 to Aurora while the side fields gave them to Dr. Mundo. Nothing agreed with anything.
audit.why: The already-written mirror audit settles it: Infected Bonesaw is 975 range on a 4s cooldown against a 900-range Q on 9s, so Mundo out-ranges AND out-cycles her poke — Levels 2-3 are genuinely his, and Aurora's real windows are Level 1 and the 4-6 stretch before Maximum Dosage. Both item stages are Mundo's. That also fits the 53.63% win rate over 1061 games.
audit.corrected: Level 1, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 to Aurora; Levels 2-3 confirmed Dr. Mundo and raised to 6/10; item stages raised to 6/10 and 7/10. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number for Between Worlds, Across the Veil or Maximum Dosage appeared anywhere, and phases[4].why argued the Mundo side on a stage the chart gives to Aurora.
audit.why: Between Worlds is 140s at rank 1 against a flat 120s Maximum Dosage, so you get your ultimate back 20 seconds sooner at every rank — that is the actual shape of the level-6 stage and the reason it stops being hers by first item. Across the Veil at 22s is the only cooldown long enough to plan a commit around.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, winCon, breakdown.mid, breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[2].d now carry 140s, 22s and the flat 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracked an ability that does not exist, with no number.
audit.why: Across the Veil 22/21/20/19/18s, The Weirding 15/14/13/12/11s, Twofold Hex 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s, Between Worlds 140/120/100s. The commit window is Across the Veil's downtime because it is both her escape and her invisibility.
audit.corrected: Rebuilt around Across the Veil and The Weirding with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Heart Zapper's heal is conditional, and nothing states that Across the Veil grants invisibility rather than just a dash.
audit.why: Riot: "If the burst hit an enemy, he heals a percentage of the stored damage" — no hit, no heal, at 325 range against a champion with a blink and a backward hop. And "entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible" means chasing the blink is chasing nothing.

notes: Three fabricated Aurora ability names on one page. "Twofold Hunt" (24 fields) is not an ability at all — the blink is Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s), and "Twofold" belongs to her Q, Twofold Hex. "Feathered Step" (4 fields) is also invented for the same W. "The Weight of Worlds" is invented for her E, which is The Weirding, and it is described as a "pull" when Riot's text is a damaging slow that hops HER backward. Plus the recurring Dr. Mundo "E stun" (6 fields) and "Q cleaver for the slow + HP refund" (5 fields), neither of which exists. CANNOT FIX: focus.text is "Aurora Twofold Hunt" at 19 characters, below the applier's 25-character floor, so the fabricated name survives on the loading-screen focus line and must be corrected by hand. Q mechanics were also wrong everywhere: the page said Twofold Hex "bounces off her passive marks"; Riot's text is a missile that curses, with a recast that drags the curses back toward her. Her passive, Spirit Abjuration, is the real heal — it exorcises spirits from everyone she damages, which is why a chip-trading pattern refills her and why the _missing file flags Grievous Wounds here. Level chart was three-way inconsistent and is now aligned to the mirror's finding that Mundo out-ranges (975 vs 900) and out-cycles (4s vs 9s) her poke at Levels 2-3.
